question.text: Ms. Anjali Desai received a drawdown notice for INR 3 crore. The PPM stipulates a 10-business-day notice period. By when must she wire the funds?

answer.text: On the date of the notice itself.
Within the 10-business-day notice period specified in the PPM.
Within 30 days of the fund year-end.

explanation.text: The Logic: The PPM's drawdown notice period governs the payment deadline. With a 10-business-day notice period, the LP must wire by the end of that 10-business-day window. Failure to wire by the deadline triggers default interest and potential forfeiture as per the PPM. The Trap: Same-day ignores the notice period. 30-day-after-year-end and 6-months are fabricated long horizons. Note: The workbook supports drawdown notices specifying the date by which payments must be made and the notice period. A precise calendar date is avoided since the source does not specify the holiday calendar. Notice-delivery commentary has been removed.
